answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with graded capability gates: before a new identity can transact, it must pass randomized, verifiable skill tests set and checked by established peers, each test costing real compute and time. Like quartz forming slowly in a frozen tundra, trust crystallizes only after sustained proof, not instant self-declaration. Every failed or copied attempt leaves an echo in the shared audit log, flagging the identity and its sponsors. Forging a thousand fake agents then means paying a thousand test costs, while one honest agent pays once.
